issues.description: The problem statement incorrectly states that the DD constructor only takes a single parameter `node: DDNode`. Both the template and solution define DD as a dataclass with two fields (node and weight), and code (in both template and solution) constructs DD objects as DD(TERM, weight) or uses DD(TERM, <complex>). This mismatch between the problem text and the actual constructor signature can confuse students about how to instantiate DDs and which helper functions/constants to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Correct the problem statement to reflect the actual DD constructor signature used in code (node and weight). For example, change the sentence to: "If you do manipulate DD objects directly, note that DD instances are constructed with both a node and a weight (DD(node, weight)). Prefer using make_dd and the predefined ONE_TERM/ZERO_TERM constants when creating DDs." This makes the textual guidance consistent with the template and solution code.
